sourceEvidence.label: Cerebro Shield endpoint source and background recovery canary

assessment.summary: The per-user collector now recovers local evidence, but trust must move off the user-controlled endpoint before the control can attest fleet coverage or prevent protected mutations.

nonNegotiables: Do not describe local hook evidence as proof of human authorization.
Do not use binary hashes or identity-provider groups as local privilege grants.
Preserve native agent integrations and bounded offline capture.
assumptions: A managed deployment can provide stable code signing, device enrollment, and an organization verification key.
No production latency, memory, fleet availability, or provider-deny measurements were supplied.

opportunities.title: Move shield trust off the user-controlled endpoint
opportunities.summary: Add remote device attestation and checkpoints, then place protected provider mutations behind an independently enforced broker.
opportunities.diagnosis: A same-user process can disable or feed the per-user collector, so local continuity and signatures protect stored evidence after capture but cannot prove complete capture or prevent a provider mutation.

evidence.claim: The LaunchAgent recovered one queued event exactly once, stayed active without the status app, and restarted after termination.
XPC admission is limited to the same effective user and the collector remains a per-user LaunchAgent.

Investigation access is short-lived, signed, device-bound, role-scoped, operation-bound, target-bound, and loaded from root-controlled configuration; adapter mutations reject a repeated local grant ID.
Complete capture and mutation prevention require an authority outside the same-user endpoint boundary.

desiredInvariants: Every enrolled device emits a signed heartbeat and monotonic receipt-chain checkpoint within policy freshness.
Missing, rolled-back, or conflicting checkpoints create an organization-visible incident.
Investigation actions require a short-lived capability bound to organization, device, subject, grant ID, canonical operation, canonical target, and expiry.
Protected provider mutations are denied unless they traverse a broker that carries a unique action identity.

options.title: Managed endpoint attestation
options.summary: Keep the per-user collector and add managed enrollment, signed heartbeats, remote chain checkpoints, and scoped investigation capabilities.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Remote freshness turns collector continuity into a fleet-visible state instead of a local observation.
Attestation detects disappearance but does not prevent a same-user bypass; the UI and policy must retain that limitation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Remote monotonic checkpoints expose missing, stale, or rolled-back endpoint evidence but do not prevent direct provider access.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Disable one enrolled collector, replay an old checkpoint, and require distinct stale and rollback incidents.

tradeoffs.assessment: Checkpointing adds one small asynchronous network request per interval outside the hook critical path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare hook p95 latency and agent CPU with 60-second checkpoints; accept under 5 ms hook delta and under 1 percent average CPU.

tradeoffs.assessment: The existing process needs only one bounded checkpoint envelope and retry record.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure steady-state RSS before and after enrollment; accept under 10 MiB increase.

tradeoffs.assessment: The existing fallback queue preserves local capture during service outages; remote retries need independent bounds and jitter.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a 24-hour offline and reconnect test and require ordered checkpoint convergence without duplicate chain heads.

tradeoffs.assessment: The organization must operate enrollment, freshness policy, incident routing, key rotation, and device retirement.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Pilot with 20 managed Macs and measure false stale alerts and time to explain an incident.

tradeoffs.assessment: The local receipt schema can remain; managed configuration and a server enrollment protocol are additive.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Enroll development and signed builds side by side while accepting checkpoints only from signed managed devices.

residualRisks: A user can still bypass hooks between checkpoints.
Direct provider credentials still permit mutations outside the endpoint evidence path.

workPackages: Add fleet freshness and rollback incidents.
acceptanceCriteria: Every enrolled test device reports freshness, chain head, and binary identity.
Disable and rollback canaries produce organization-visible incidents within policy time.
migrationNotes: Reject organization-managed status for ad-hoc builds.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable remote checkpoint delivery while retaining the local collector and ledger.

options.title: Brokered provider enforcement
options.summary: Add remote attestation, a privileged local policy boundary where needed, and provider-side deny rules that allow protected mutations only through a dedicated broker.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A separately authorized boundary can resist same-user disablement for the protected paths it owns.
Provider deny policy makes the independent authority own mutation prevention rather than endpoint observation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Provider deny removes direct protected mutation paths and the broker binds each allowed mutation to an action identity.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Attempt protected mutations through broker, normal user credentials, stale device state, forged action IDs, and break-glass roles.

tradeoffs.assessment: Protected actions gain a network authorization and broker hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark provider action p50 and p95; set a service-specific latency budget before rollout.

tradeoffs.assessment: Broker and optional privileged endpoint service add process and queue memory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Load-test broker concurrency and measure privileged service steady-state RSS.

tradeoffs.assessment: Broker unavailability can deny protected work by design, so bounded fail-closed behavior and break-glass controls become production dependencies.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run regional outage, retry, duplicate request, and break-glass exercises.

tradeoffs.assessment: This option adds provider policy rollout, broker on-call, audit retention, exception governance, and privileged software distribution.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete a service ownership and incident-response review before enabling denies.

tradeoffs.assessment: Credentials and automation must move behind the broker before provider deny can be enabled safely.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inventory protected call paths, run report-only policy, then canary deny one non-production scope.

residualRisks: Break-glass identities can bypass the broker and must remain in the provider-event denominator.
Unprotected local and provider actions remain observable rather than prevented.

workPackages: Deploy report-only then enforced provider policy.
acceptanceCriteria: All protected brokered mutations bind one-to-one.
All deliberate direct-role canaries are denied or appear as governed break-glass events.
migrationNotes: Begin with one sandbox resource family and preserve emergency access.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable the deny statement and revoke broker issuance while retaining audit events.

opportunities.recommendation: Ship managed remote attestation first to measure fleet coverage; require brokered provider enforcement before claiming prevention for any protected mutation.

openQuestions: Which provider mutations and local processes are important enough to justify fail-closed enforcement?
What freshness window and offline allowance match the managed Mac population?
Who owns broker availability and break-glass review?
